question: What will be the value of elasticity of demand (e_D) in the demand curve having the shape of rectangular hyperbola?
solution:
The correct answer is __**∣eD​∣=1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A demand curve in the shape of a rectangular hyperbola implies that the product of price and quantity demanded is constant at all points along the curve.
 
• When the demand curve is a rectangular hyperbola, it means the elasticity of demand (e_D) is unitary, i.e., |e_D| = 1.
 
• This characteristic suggests that a percentage change in price results in an equal and opposite percentage change in quantity demanded, maintaining total expenditure constant.
 
• Rectangular hyperbola demand curves are often used to represent perfectly competitive markets where total revenue remains unchanged regardless of price changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elasticity of Demand (e_D)**

 
 
• Elasticity of demand measures how much the quantity demanded of a good responds to a change in the price of that good.
 
• The formula for calculating price elasticity of demand is: e_D = (% Change in Quantity Demanded) / (% Change in Price).
 
• If |e_D| > 1, demand is elastic, meaning consumers are highly responsive to price changes.

• **Rectangular Hyperbola**
 
 
• A rectangular hyperbola is a type of hyperbola where the product of the coordinates of any point on the curve is a constant.
 
• In the context of demand curves, it represents a situation where the product of price (P) and quantity demanded (Q) is constant (P * Q = k).
 
• This implies that the total revenue (P * Q) remains unchanged at different points along the curve.
 
• Such a curve is used to illustrate markets where a change in price does not affect total expenditure on the good.
